nodes.title: Cellular Respiration Overview

body.summary: Overall cellular respiration equation: Glucose + 6 O2 -> 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + energy (ATP) | Three stages of cellular respiration: Glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain.

nodes.quote: Overall cellular respiration equation: Glucose + 6 O2 -> 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + energy (ATP)

nodes.title: Glycolysis

body.summary: Glycolysis location and oxygen requirement: Happens in the cytosol and does not need oxygen. | Glycolysis net yield per glucose: 2 ATP and 2 NADH (starting with one 6C glucose becoming two 3C pyruvate).

nodes.quote: Glycolysis location and oxygen requirement: Happens in the cytosol and does not need oxygen.

nodes.title: Krebs Cycle

body.summary: Krebs cycle location: In the mitochondrial matrix. | Krebs cycle yields per glucose: 2 ATP, 6 NADH, 2 FADH2, and 4 CO2 released. | Can you explain the main role of the Krebs cycle and where it occurs? (Occurs in the mitochondrial matrix; Takes in Acetyl-CoA; Produces electron carriers like NADH and FADH2 along with ATP and CO2)

nodes.quote: Krebs cycle location: In the mitochondrial matrix.

nodes.title: Electron Transport Chain

body.summary: Electron transport chain location: Inner mitochondrial membrane. | ETC ATP yield: About 26-28 ATP driven by chemiosmosis and ATP synthase. | How do the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis work together to generate ATP? (NADH and FADH2 donate electrons to the chain located on the inner mitochondrial membrane; Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor; Chemiosmosis drives ATP synthase to yield about 26-28 ATP)

nodes.quote: Electron transport chain location: Inner mitochondrial membrane.

nodes.title: Fermentation

body.summary: Types of fermentation without oxygen: Lactic acid fermentation (muscle) and alcohol fermentation (yeast). | Purpose of fermentation: Regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can continue without oxygen.

nodes.quote: Types of fermentation without oxygen: Lactic acid fermentation (muscle) and alcohol fermentation (yeast).
